units: <cite ref="Berakhot 6b:9">Ber. 6ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>פ׳ גסה</he>, v. <cite ref="C01161"><he>גַּס</he> III</cite>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 39:9">Gen. R. s. 39</cite> <he>ליתן שכר על כל פ׳ ופ׳</he> to reward him for every step.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 7:2:5">Koh. R. to VII, 2</cite> ‘and the living shall take it to heart’ (<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 7:2:5">ib.</cite>) <he>זה חי העולמים … על כל פ׳ ופ׳ וכ׳</he> that means the Everliving who rewards man for every step he takes for deeds of charity.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 33:1">Pesik. R. s. 33</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 51:14">Is. LI, 14</cite>) <he>מן אדם שהוא ממהר בפְסִיעָתוֹ בשביל להיפתח וכ׳</he> art thou afraid of man who hastens his step to have an opening … and runs with hasty step, that he may not miss his bread?; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 336">Yalk. Is. 336</cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>פְּסִיעוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Yoma 53b:2">Yoma 53ᵇ</cite> <he>המתפלל צריך שיפסיע שלש פ׳ לאחוריו וכ׳</he> he who is in prayer (when a person enters), must pass three steps backward (when he ends his prayer), and then turn around to salute.
<cite ref="Yoma 53b:5">Ib.</cite> <he>דפסעי להו שלש פ׳ בכריעה אחת</he> they made the three steps back ward with one bow.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 22a:19">Snh. 22ᵃ</cite> (he who loses his wife) <he>פְּסִיעוֹתָיו מתקצרות</he> has his steps shortened (his energies broken, with ref. to <cite ref="Job 18:7">Job XVIII, 7</cite>).
<cite ref="Shabbat 63b:13">Sabb. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>שהיו פְסִיעוֹתֵיהֶם גסות</he> who used to make wide steps.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 4:20">Num. R. s. 4</cite>; a. fr.
